claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. 

To get started, could you tell me the **name(s) of the child or children** you'd like me to assess eligibility for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I have one child - Alex. I wanted to check if I can claim Child Benefit for them?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that context. Let me start assessing your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

First, I need to gather some key information. Let me ask you:

**How old is Alex?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. To continue the assessment, I need to understand your living situation with Alex.

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good, thank you. Now I need to check a few more important details about your circumstances.

**Are you responsible for financially supporting Alex (for example, do you provide food, clothing, and accommodation)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I am responsible for Alex - I provide everything they need, food, clothes, and a home.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. Before I can make a final determination, I need to check one more important thing about your residency status.

**Are you a British citizen, or do you have a right to reside in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, I don't live in the UK at the moment. I'm living abroad right now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that important information. That does affect the eligibility assessment.

Before I make my final determination, I need to clarify one more detail:

**Does Alex live with you abroad, or does Alex remain in the UK with someone else?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. Let me now check the official eligibility rules to make sure I give you an accurate assessment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the official eligibility rules I've reviewed, I can now provide you with my assessment.

The key issue for your eligibility is that you are currently living abroad with Alex. According to the Child Benefit eligibility rules, you normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child under 16 and **you live in the UK**.

The rules do state that "You may be able to get Child Benefit if you go to live in certain countries or if you're a Crown servant," but this requires you to meet specific conditions relating to certain countries and special circumstances.

Since you've indicated that you're living abroad and Alex also lives with you abroad, and without knowing your specific Crown servant status or whether you're in one of the qualifying countries, you would not meet the standard eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Summary of the outcome:**

Unfortunately, you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex at this time. The primary reason is that Child Benefit requires you to live in the UK, and you are currently living abroad.

However, if any of the following apply to you, I'd recommend contacting HMRC to discuss your specific circumstances further:
- You are a Crown servant
- You plan to move back to the UK
- You believe you may qualify for an exception under the rules for certain countries

Is there anything else I can help clarify for you?
